answer: A staking-and-reputation inlet throttles new agents: each identity must lock a refundable bond that grows with the value it touches, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital per identity. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a dune, reputation accrues only through verified, paid work over time, and misbehavior slashes the bond. An attacker must fund every fake identity and wait out the same slow trust curve, turning a cheap flood into an expensive, slow grind.
